earlier_scan.source_named: Drabbe, P. 1950. Spraakkunst van den Awju-taal (BKI); SIL survey Kriens & Lebold 2010 also exists but SIL returned HTTP 403

new_statements.quote: The only difference between the sound systems of Syiagha-Yenimu and Sawuy is the probable presence of a sixth vowel, ɛ, in Syiagha-Yenimu. Minor differences on the allophonic level may exist, but the very global phonetic description by Drabbe does not allow to go into details. Supra-segmentals: stress, but no rules of stress placement have been given.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE CHECK. Voorhoeve 1975, PL C-38, p. 375 (PDF page 31 of; page image, viewed): sec. 2.6.2.2.6.2.2 'Syiagha-Yenimu' ends exactly "The only difference between the sound systems of Syiagha-Yenimu and Sawuy is the probable presence of a sixth vowel, ɛ, in Syiagha-Yenimu. Minor differences on the allophonic level may exist, but the very global phonetic description by Drabbe does not allow to go into details. Supra-segmentals: stress, but no rules of stress placement have been given." Verbatim. Same section: "There are two dialects, Syiagha, and Yenimu. The data presented below represent the Syiagha dialect... Drabbe (1950a) published a grammatical sketch of Syiagha-Yenimu, including a wordli…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Second-hand only: Voorhoeve's survey, summarising Drabbe 1950a (the only description; data = Syiagha dialect), says the language has stress but that the primary source gives no rule for where it falls. No placement rule is available from any opened source. (For comparison, the same survey gives Aghu 'weak stress on the last syllable of monomorphemic words' and Sawuy 'last syllable usually carries the main stress', but says nothing of the kind for Syiagha-Yenimu.)
new_statements.exceptions: none; Wester 2014 (Table 3.2) reports only that in endocentric noun compounds the first (modifying) noun carries the stress, Shiaxa included, Yenimu lacking data.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level implied ('stress placement'); no discussion of citation forms vs phrases.
new_statements.identity_note: Voorhoeve 1975's data 'represent the Syiagha dialect' of Syiagha-Yenimu (= South Awyu, sout2941, also called Oser; Glottolog lists no dialect children but links Lexibank 'Syiagha' and 'Yenimu' wordlists). Drabbe 1950 covers both dialects; Yenimu is the less described. Not to be confused with Drabbe 1957 (Aghu, aghu1254), Drabbe 1947 (Pisa = Asue Awyu, unpublished KITLV ms.) or Drabbe 1959 (Kaeti/Wambon, Dumut).
